guard: resolved manager command count is derived from the shipped cluster document, not restated; and the contract module compiles on first use, not at import
why: Reached suites used to pin 18 while the shipped document served 20. Restating the count is the
defect class: correct the day it is written, wrong after the next served command.
M1 puts the restated 18 back into managerShippedSurface. The invoke cell compares live resolve
size to that count, so it goes red on the named mismatch. Unique code-only return, not a comment.
M2 restores revision 15 after self-targeted run-answer is the next shipped command change. The
new command mode and grant ship together, so 15 would name the preceding surface. The
named revision cell runs after the service has published and a generic client has resolved the
M3 re-introduces the module-scope compile (#1323): every CLI invocation paid ~1.8 CPU-seconds
of Ajv work before its verb was read. The lazy Proxy is replaced by an eager map built at
import, the exact shape the fix removed. The contract-vocabulary import-cost cell measures the
module's CPU cost over its dependency floor in fresh children, so the eager compile trips it
by ~7x the bound while the lazy module sits 3-6x under it.
